blocks.text: Organizing your browser for travel agency work

Travel agents live in their browsers. When you have dozens of tabs open for GDS systems, hotel portals, and flight aggregators, Chrome can become a mess. Start by using Chrome profiles to keep your work and personal life separate. Go to your profile icon in the top right corner and select Add to create a new profile for specific clients or suppliers. This keeps your cookies and history clean.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for travel agents

Speed matters when you are finalizing a booking. Use ⌘ + T to open a new tab instantly. Use ⌘ + L to jump to the address bar. If you need to switch between active tabs, use ⌘ + Option + Right Arrow. These small movements save minutes every hour. You can also create custom shortcuts for menu items in System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > App Shortcuts if you find yourself clicking the same menu items repeatedly.

When you are looking at a complex itinerary on a website, hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur about the details. You can ask, What is the layover time for this flight? or Does this hotel policy include breakfast? Lazur sees your screen and answers out loud. This stops you from having to switch windows or copy-paste text into a separate document.

Researching new destinations often leads to tab overload. Instead of opening twenty tabs, ask Lazur to perform the research for you. Lazur uses its own background tabs to gather information and provides a summary. You keep your main browser window clean for active bookings. This approach prevents the browser from slowing down due to memory usage.

Email is a massive part of a travel agent's day. Use the fn key to dictate quick replies directly into Gmail or your CRM. Because Lazur formats the text as you speak, you can send professional responses to clients without typing. This is helpful when you are on a call and need to log notes or send a quick update simultaneously.
Troubleshooting Chrome when it slows down

Sometimes Chrome will freeze during a critical booking. First, check your extensions. Go to Chrome > Settings > Extensions and remove anything you do not use daily. Extensions are a common cause of browser instability. If a specific site fails to load, try clearing the cache for that site only. You can also use the Task Manager in Chrome by going to Window > Task Manager to see which tab is using the most memory.

Security is mandatory when handling passport details and credit card numbers. Never save passwords in clear text. Use a dedicated password manager. In Chrome, ensure you are using the Google Password Manager and keep your browser updated. Go to Chrome > About Google Chrome to check your version. If you are on an older macOS, you might be stuck on an older version of Chrome, which puts your client data at risk.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons on booking websites for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps. It points at things, answers questions, and guides you, but you perform the final interaction.

faq.question: Does Lazur store my client data?
faq.answer: No. Lazur only sees your screen when you hold the shortcut key. The data is not stored or used to train AI models.

faq.question: How do I speed up Chrome on my Mac?
faq.answer: Close unused tabs, remove unnecessary extensions, and keep your browser updated to the latest version.
